newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand says mulls measures to boost revenue.
newsitem.headline: Thailand says mulls measures to boost revenue.

text.p: Thai Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan said on Tuesday the government was considering measures to raise revenue which has declined due to the country's sluggish economy.
Amnuay, speaking after meeting with the government agencies involving in tax collection, did not give details.
"The slowing economy has significantly affected government revenue. We are finding measures to solve the decline in revenue collection," Amnuay told reporters.

Thailand recorded a fiscal deficit of 53.75 billion baht ($2.07 billion) in the first six months of fiscal 1996-97 (October-September) due to lower-than-expected revenue caused by a slowing of the economy, the finance ministry said last month.
Amnuay said the government had no plan to cut spending for the 1996/97 fiscal year after the government made substantial reductions earlier this year.
The government in February announced that it would cut the 1996/97 budget by 99 billion baht as part of an attempt to cope with lower-than-expected revenue collection. ($1 = 26 baht)
